stages.title: Advanced vocabulary and terminology
stages.hook: Many abstract Russian nouns are built from adjectives or verbs. How is "ответственность" built?
explain: Abstract vocabulary is often made with suffixes. The suffix -ость turns an adjective into a quality: ответственный (responsible) gives ответственность, возможный gives возможность. The suffixes -ие and -ение make nouns from verbs: достичь gives достижение (achievement), влиять gives влияние.

Abstract nouns are typical of the book style used in articles and exams: обстоятельство (circumstance), последствие (consequence), тенденция (trend), условие (condition). Beware of false friends: актуальный means topical or relevant, not "actual", and ситуация is used for any situation.
stages.mnemonic: -ость makes a quality: responsible becomes responsibility.
sentences: This has a great influence on society.
We must take all circumstances into account.

gq.q: Which noun comes from the adjective возможный?
gq.why: The suffix -ость forms nouns of quality from adjectives.

gq.q: What does актуальный usually mean in Russian?
gq.why: It is a false friend of English "actual".

panel.q: Why are abstract nouns frequent in academic Russian?
o: They compress actions and qualities into noun phrases, typical of the book style
They are only used in poems
panel.why: Nominal style is characteristic of formal writing.

panel.q: Which pair shows a register contrast?
panel.why: Choosing the verb sets the tone.

panel.q: Why learn word families such as влиять, влияние, влиятельный?
o: One root connects several parts of speech, widening vocabulary
panel.why: Derivation lets you guess related forms.

teach.model: Abstract nouns are built with suffixes: -ость from adjectives and -ие or -ение from verbs. They belong to the book style. Watch for false friends like актуальный.

trip.prompt: Find derivation patterns and make three new nouns from adjectives.

stages.title: Academic language
stages.hook: In an academic Russian text the writer rarely says "I". How is it written instead?
explain: Academic Russian prefers impersonal forms. Instead of Мы провели исследование a text says Было проведено исследование, using a short passive participle. Short participles also appear in Работа выполнена and Данные были проанализированы.

Key terms are исследование (research), гипотеза (hypothesis), метод (method), данные (data), анализ (analysis) and источник (source). Cite or report with Согласно данным..., По мнению автора... and Автор утверждает, что... Make claims carefully with Можно предположить, что... (One may suppose that...).
stages.mnemonic: The text, not the writer, stands on the stage: было проведено.
sentences: The author claims that the method is effective.

gq.why: The impersonal passive is typical of academic style.

gq.q: Which phrase reports someone else's view?
gq.why: По мнению means in the opinion of.

panel.q: Why do academic texts avoid "I"?
o: Russian has no first person form of the verb
Authors are not allowed to exist
They aim for an objective, impersonal tone
panel.why: Impersonal forms emphasise results over the writer.

panel.q: What does Можно предположить, что... achieve?
o: It gives a strict order to the reader
It states a fact with certainty
It presents a claim with caution

panel.q: What does a short passive participle (выполнена) show?
o: The state or result of an action
A future event that has not happened
panel.why: It agrees in gender with the subject: работа выполнена.

teach.model: Academic Russian uses impersonal forms and short passive participles: Было проведено исследование. Key terms are гипотеза, метод, данные and анализ. Hedge claims with Можно предположить, что...

points.ask: How do I make careful claims?

trip.prompt: Find a Russian scientific abstract and mark the passive forms.

stages.title: Professional communication
stages.hook: What would you write in the first line of an e-mail to a company that you want to join?
explain: Professional Russian is polite and clear. A job application includes the резюме (CV) and a short letter: Прошу рассмотреть мою кандидатуру на должность менеджера (I ask you to consider my candidacy for the position of manager). Interviews are called собеседования.

At work, meetings (совещания) have deadlines (сроки). Use set phrases like в связи с (in connection with), в соответствии с договором (in accordance with the contract) and Направляю вам... (I am sending you...). Start e-mails with Добрый день, name and patronymic, and end with С уважением, name.
stages.mnemonic: Прошу + infinitive: the formal key to a request.
sentences: I ask you to consider my application.
The meeting will begin at ten o'clock.
The deadline for the project is Friday.

gq.q: Which opening fits a business e-mail?
What does в связи с mean?
gq.why: It is a formal preposition followed by the instrumental.

panel.q: Why is Прошу рассмотреть more suitable than Рассмотрите?
o: It is shorter and sounds much friendlier
It is a formal request, not a command
panel.why: Прошу plus an infinitive is a polite formula.

panel.q: Which choice is best for a colleague you know well, in a team chat?
o: Уважаемый коллега, позвольте обратить ваше внимание
panel.why: Register should match the relationship and channel.

panel.q: Why is a резюме usually short?
o: Russian has no words for long documents
Readers scan it quickly for key facts

teach.model: Use formal formulas: Прошу рассмотреть, Направляю вам and С уважением. Keep a polite register, mention deadlines clearly, and use set phrases like в связи с.

points.ask: How do I make a formal request?
How do I start and end an e-mail?

trip.prompt: Look at a model CV and list the sections.

stages.title: Literary analysis
stages.hook: Chekhov's characters often say little. What do readers learn from what is not said?
explain: Literary analysis names devices: метафора (metaphor), символ (symbol), конфликт (conflict), повествователь (narrator), композиция (structure) and подтекст (subtext). In Chekhov's Вишнёвый сад the orchard symbolises the past; characters talk about everyday things while deeper feelings stay in the подтекст.

The "superfluous man" (лишний человек) is a type found in Pushkin's Онегин and Lermontov's Герой нашего времени: an educated man who feels without purpose. In Dostoevsky's Преступление и наказание the central conflict is inside Raskolnikov. A narrator can tell the story от первого лица (in the first person) or from outside.
stages.mnemonic: What is said is the tip; the подтекст is the iceberg.
sentences: There is a strong conflict in the novel.
The narrator tells the story in the first person.

gq.q: What does the orchard symbolise in Chekhov's Вишнёвый сад?
o: The past and a way of life that is passing
gq.why: The orchard represents the old order and memory.
Crime and Punishment is by Fyodor Dostoevsky.

panel.q: What is подтекст?
o: A footnote at the bottom of the page

panel.q: What is a "superfluous man" in Russian literature?
o: An educated character who finds no purpose in society

panel.q: Why does a first-person narrator limit the story?
o: Readers see only what that narrator knows and feels
panel.why: Narrative point of view shapes what we learn.

teach.model: Name devices such as метафора, символ, конфликт and подтекст. In Вишнёвый сад the orchard symbolises the past. The narrator can speak от первого лица. A лишний человек is a hero without purpose.

trip.prompt: Read the plot summary and find one symbol.

stages.title: Advanced listening comprehension
stages.hook: Spoken Russian changes sounds at word boundaries. How is "в школе" actually pronounced?
explain: Advanced listening means following the gist (суть) first and details (подробности) next. Sounds change in connected speech. A voiced consonant before a voiceless one becomes voiceless: в школе sounds like "fshkole". The ending -ться in verbs is pronounced "tsa": учиться sounds like "uchitsa".

Speakers use pauses (паузы) and tempo (темп) to organise meaning. Slips of the tongue (оговорки) and interruptions are normal. Tongue twisters (скороговорки) such as Карл у Клары украл кораллы train difficult sound sequences.
sentences: He speaks at a fast tempo.

gq.q: How is the ending -ться in учиться pronounced?
gq.why: Тся and ться are both pronounced as a single "tsa".

gq.q: What is the best first step in listening to a fast speaker?
o: Write down every single sound you hear
Catch the gist and stressed words
Stop at the first unknown word

panel.q: Why is в школе pronounced "fshkole"?
o: A voiced consonant becomes voiceless before a voiceless one

panel.q: Why do learners misunderstand spoken forms they know in writing?
o: Reduction and assimilation make speech differ from spelling
panel.why: Sound changes are not shown in spelling.

panel.q: What do tongue twisters train?
o: Fast, accurate movement through difficult sound sequences

teach.model: First catch the gist, then the details. Sounds change in speech: в школе sounds like fshkole and -ться is pronounced tsa. Use pauses and stress to find the structure.

trip.prompt: Find the voicing assimilation section and read three examples aloud.

stages.title: Oral fluency and presentations
stages.hook: You lose your train of thought while speaking. Which phrases let you keep going smoothly?
explain: Fluent speakers use discourse phrases. Иными словами (in other words) restates, Что касается... (as for...) shifts the topic, Как я уже говорил (as I have already said) refers back and Подводя итог (summing up) closes. Что касается is followed by the genitive: Что касается цены.

Подводя итог contains a gerund (деепричастие), a verb form that expresses an action accompanying the main one. To stay fluent, pause calmly, avoid too many fillers like значит and как бы, and use rising and falling intonation to mark ideas.
stages.mnemonic: Signposts keep both speaker and listener on the road.
items: Let us move to the next question.
sentences: In other words, this is impossible.
As for the price, it is high.
Summing up, I will say the following.

gq.why: Подводя is a gerund accompanying the main action.

panel.q: Why do speakers use phrases like иными словами?
o: They restate an idea to help the listener

panel.q: What is a risk of using too many fillers?
o: The speech sounds hesitant and loses force

panel.q: Which strategy supports fluency?
o: Short pauses and clear intonation to mark ideas

teach.model: Use signposts: иными словами, что касается, как я уже говорил and подводя итог. Что касается takes the genitive. Use pauses and intonation, and avoid too many fillers.

trip.prompt: Watch a short talk and note two signpost phrases.

stages.title: Translation and interpretation
stages.hook: An interpreter listens and speaks at the same time. How is that different from translating a book?
explain: Translation (перевод) works with written text and time to revise. Interpretation (устный перевод) is done live: последовательный (consecutive) waits for the speaker to pause, and синхронный (simultaneous) follows the speaker with a delay of a few seconds. Both need concentration, terminology and quick decisions.

A калька (calque) is a copy of a foreign structure in word-for-word form and often sounds unnatural. Skilled translators convey the nuance (нюанс) and register. Ethics matter: faithfulness to meaning, neutrality and confidentiality.
stages.mnemonic: Consecutive waits, simultaneous runs: both carry meaning.
sentences: The interpreter conveys meaning, not words.

o: The interpreter speaks at the same time as the speaker
The interpreter speaks after the speaker pauses
The interpreter repeats the same sentence
A word-for-word copy of a foreign structure

panel.q: Why is confidentiality part of an interpreter's ethics?
o: Interpreters hear private or sensitive information
panel.why: Trust is essential to the profession.

panel.q: What does a translator do when a term has no direct equivalent?
o: Chooses an explanation or closest accepted term and stays consistent

panel.q: Why are glossaries prepared before simultaneous interpreting?
o: Speakers read the glossaries aloud to the audience
There is little time to search for terms live
panel.why: Preparation saves time during the event.

teach.model: Translators work with written text; interpreters work live. Consecutive interpreting follows pauses, and simultaneous interpreting runs a few seconds behind. Avoid calques and keep terminology consistent.

points.ask: What types of interpreting are there?

trip.prompt: Read about modes of interpretation and note one difference.

stages.title: Idiomatic and figurative language
stages.hook: Russians say "making an elephant out of a fly". What does that mean?
explain: Figurative language gives colourful meaning. Делать из мухи слона means to exaggerate, Медвежья услуга (a bear's service) is help that causes harm, Как снег на голову (like snow on the head) means suddenly and unexpectedly, and Вешать лапшу на уши means to deceive someone with false stories.

Other expressions: Убить двух зайцев (to kill two hares) is to achieve two aims at once, Быть на седьмом небе means to be extremely happy, and Дело в шляпе means the job is done. Idioms often come from folk life, fables and Russian history, and each must be learned as a whole.
stages.mnemonic: Each idiom is a tiny picture: elephant, bear, snow, hare.
items: to achieve two aims at once
sentences: His arrival was a complete surprise.
He achieved two aims at once.

gq.why: The idiom describes a well-meant but harmful act.
Snow on the head is a sudden event.

panel.q: Why should idioms be learned as wholes?
o: Their meaning cannot be derived from the separate words
panel.why: An idiom is a fixed unit.

panel.q: How would you translate делать из мухи слона into English?
o: Make an elephant from a fly literally
Make a mountain out of a molehill
panel.why: A good translation uses an equivalent English idiom.

panel.q: Which context fits быть на седьмом небе?
o: Missing a train and being angry
Winning a prize you dreamed of

teach.model: Idioms such as делать из мухи слона and как снег на голову are fixed pictures with their own meaning. Translate them by meaning, not word by word, and learn each as a whole.

trip.prompt: Pick two Russian idioms and find English equivalents.

stages.title: Extended independent writing
stages.hook: A long essay needs a thread that guides the reader. What words in Russian make that thread visible?
explain: Independent writing needs a clear thesis, supporting paragraphs and links between them. Useful devices: в первую очередь (first of all), следует отметить (it should be noted), вместе с тем (at the same time), в результате (as a result), исходя из этого (on this basis) and в целом (on the whole).

Keep the style consistent and formal. Prefer varied sentence length, avoid repeating the same word, and check agreement of adjectives and cases. After writing, revise: test each paragraph for one main idea, cut unnecessary words and read aloud for rhythm.
stages.mnemonic: Thesis, evidence, link, conclusion: a thread through the essay.
sentences: It should be noted that the problem is complex.
On this basis a conclusion can be drawn.
On the whole the work deserves attention.

gq.why: В результате means as a result.

gq.q: Which case follows это свидетельствует о?
gq.why: The preposition о takes the prepositional case here: о росте.

panel.q: Why use linking phrases between paragraphs?
o: They show how ideas relate and guide the reader

panel.q: What is the purpose of revision?
o: To improve clarity, unity and style after a first draft

panel.q: Which sentence is more suitable for a formal essay?
o: Ну, в общем, результаты как бы получились разные

teach.model: State a thesis, support it in paragraphs and link them with phrases like в первую очередь, вместе с тем and в результате. Keep a formal style and revise your draft.

points.ask: What do I do after writing?

trip.prompt: Read a model essay outline and mark the linking phrases.
